We imaged L4 cells in Scnna1-Cre mice. We imaged from 107 responsive cells in L4 of NH mice (six imaging fields, five mice, 322 total cells, age: P70 ± 16). We found that the point representation was sharper in L4 than L2/3 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2C and citations to prior studies.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, enrichment reduced mean whisker-evoked responses in L4 for cells in most bins <375 μm from the reference whisker's column center (p<0.05 for each bin).
claims.source: In EN mice, we imaged from 181 responsive cells in L4 (eight imaging fields, six mice, 586 total cells, age: P58 ± 5). We found that EN reduced mean whisker-evoked responses for cells in most bins <375 μm from the reference whisker's column center (p<0.05 for each bin), including at 0–75 μm (NH: 1.11 ± 0.13, EN: 0.86 ± 0.06, p=0.034) (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Enrichment generally weakened L4 whisker responses, rather than sharpening the point representation relative to its central peak.
claims.source: Thus, enrichment generally weakened L4 whisker responses, rather than sharpening the point representation relative to its central peak.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the L4 data in Figure 2C-D.

claims.claim: Enrichment did not alter mean barrel radius in Drd3-Cre mice (NH: 151 ± 7.2 μm, EN: 145 ± 4.6 μm, p=0.7).
claims.source: Enrichment did not alter mean barrel radius (NH: 151 ± 7.2 μm, n = 6 mice, EN: 145 ± 4.6 μm [mean ± SEM], n = 7 mice (2-way ANOVA, factors: enrichment and barrel identity, p=0.7 for enrichment factor) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from anatomical measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Enrichment did not alter barrel radius in Scnn1a-Cre mice (NH: 118 ± 6.6 μm, EN: 124 ± 6.9 μm, p=0.01).
claims.source: There was also no change in barrel radius in Scnn1a-Cre mice, which have a slightly smaller barrels (NH: 118 ± 6.6 μm, n = 5 mice, EN: 124 ± 6.9 μm, n = 6 mice, p=0.01 for enrichment factor).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from anatomical measurements.

claims.claim: The functional changes in L2/3 point representation occurred without gross changes in L4 barrel dimensions.
claims.source: Thus, the functional changes in L2/3 point representation occurred without gross changes in L4 barrel dimensions.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the barrel size measurements in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: 53% of responsive L2/3 cells within 0–75 µm of a column center in normally housed mice had a best whisker that matched the columnar whisker.
claims.source: 53% (31/58) of responsive cells within 0–75 µm of a column center had a BW that matched the column's anatomically-mapped whisker (termed the columnar whisker, CW).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from tuning analysis in normally housed mice.

claims.claim: 67% of L2/3 PYR cells within 0–75 µm of the column center in normally housed mice were tuned to the columnar whisker using the statistically equivalent best whisker criterion.
claims.source: By this measure, 67% (39/58) of L2/3 PYR cells within 0–75 µm of the column center were tuned to the CW.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from tuning analysis using the eBW criterion.

claims.claim: 63% of L4 excitatory cells in normally housed mice had a best whisker that matched the columnar whisker.
claims.source: 63% of L4 excitatory cells (30/48) had a BW that matched the CW, and 73% (35/48) had the CW among the eBWs.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis.

claims.claim: The fraction of cells tuned to a given whisker fell off approximately 30% more sharply with distance in L4 than in L2/3.
claims.source: However, the fraction of cells tuned to a given whisker fell off ~30% more sharply with distance in L4 than in L2/3, using either tuning measure. This difference was significant at distance bins from 150 to 375 µm from the column center (p<0.05, Fisher's Exact Test) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between L2/3 and L4 shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: L4 exhibits more topographic precision in whisker tuning of single cells than L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, L4 exhibits more topographic precision in whisker tuning of single cells than L2/3.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of tuning precision between L2/3 and L4.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, 82% of L2/3 cells located 0–75 μm from a column center were tuned to the columnar whisker, which is greater than in normally housed mice (67%, p=0.025).
claims.source: In EN mice, 82% (111/135) of cells located 0–75 μm from a column center were tuned to the CW, which is greater than NH mice (67%, p=0.025, Fisher's Exact Test).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing enriched and normally housed mice shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: 77.1% of whisker-responsive cells within column boundaries in enriched mice were tuned to the columnar whisker, compared to 65.1% in normally housed mice (p=0.00008).
claims.source: When all cells located within column boundaries were considered together (irrespective of distance to center), 77.1% (468/607) of whisker-responsive cells in EN mice were tuned to the CW, compared to 65.1% (224/344) in NH (p=0.00008).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result showing enrichment increased tuning precision.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased L2/3 map precision, particularly in the home column of each whisker, but did not abolish salt-and-pepper tuning.
claims.source: Thus, EN increased L2/3 map precision, particularly in the home column of each whisker, but did not abolish salt-and-pepper tuning (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tuning data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, 90% of L4 cells at column centers (0–75 μm) were tuned to the columnar whisker, which is greater than the 73% in normally housed mice (p=0.021).
claims.source: In EN mice, 90% (57/63) of cells at column centers (0–75 μm) were tuned to the CW, which is greater than the 73% in NH mice (p=0.021) (Figure 3C–D).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, 89.3% of all L4 cells within a column boundary were columnar whisker-tuned, compared to 75.6% in normally housed mice (p=0.0086).
claims.source: In EN mice, 89.3% (133/149) of all cells within a column boundary were CW-tuned, compared to 75.6% (65/86) in NH mice (p=0.0086).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased tuning precision in L4.
claims.source: Thus, despite the expectation that L4 is less plastic than L2/3 (Glazewski and Fox, 1996; Feldman and Brecht, 2005), enrichment also increased tuning precision in L4.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on L4 tuning data, with citations to prior work on L4 plasticity.

claims.claim: In L2/3, enrichment increased responses to the strongest three whiskers and decreased responses to the weakest three whiskers, relative to normally housed cells.
claims.source: In L2/3, EN increased responses to the strongest three whiskers, and decreased responses to the weakest three whiskers, relative to NH cells (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by rank-ordered receptive field data in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Receptive fields were sharper, on average, in enriched mice compared to normally housed mice in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, receptive fields were sharper, on average, in EN mice.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rank-ordered receptive field analysis in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased the signal-to-noise of both columnar whisker response and the best 2 surround whisker responses in L2/3.
claims.source: EN specifically increased the signal-to-noise of both CW response and the best 2 SW responses (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Enrichment decreased spontaneous (blank trial) activity relative to normally housed mice in L2/3.
claims.source: In addition to these changes in tuning shape, EN also decreased spontaneous (blank trial) activity relative to NH (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Columnar whisker responses were higher in enriched than normally housed mice in L2/3 (NH: 0.64 ± 0.03, EN: 0.71 ± 0.02; p=0.01).
claims.source: CW responses were higher in EN than NH (NH: 0.64 ± 0.03, EN: 0.71 ± 0.02; p=0.01, permutation test for difference in means).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis in L2/3.

claims.claim: Enrichment reduced responses to the surround whisker one row dorsal to the columnar whisker in L2/3 (within-arc, −1 row: NH: 0.44 ± 0.02, EN 0.35 ± 0.02, p=0.001).
claims.source: EN reduced responses to both these SWs (within-arc, −1 row: NH: 0.44 ± 0.02, EN 0.35 ± 0.02, p=0.001; within-arc, +one row: NH: 0.39 ± 0.02, EN: 0.29 ± 0.01, p=0.0001).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased responses to the surround whisker one arc rostral of the columnar whisker in L2/3 (within-row, +one arc: NH: 0.34 ± 0.01, EN: 0.53 ± 0.02, p=0.0001).
claims.source: In the within-row dimension, EN increased responses to the SW one arc rostral of the CW (within-row, +one arc: NH: 0.34 ± 0.01, EN: 0.53 ± 0.02, p=0.0001), and did not alter responses to the SW one arc caudal of the CW (within-row, −1 arc: NH: 0.57 ± 0.04, EN 0.55 ± 0.04, p=0.40).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Enrichment broadened receptive fields in the within-row dimension in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, EN broadened receptive fields in the within-row dimension (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the receptive field data in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: In L4, enrichment reduced responses to most whiskers in rank-ordered receptive fields.
claims.source: In L4, EN reduced responses to most whiskers in rank-ordered receptive fields (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4A for L4.

claims.claim: In L4, responses to the best surround whisker were reduced somewhat more than responses to the columnar whisker by enrichment.
claims.source: Responses to the best surround whisker were reduced somewhat more than responses to the CW (Figure 4A–B), and spontaneous activity was unaffected (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4A-C for L4.

claims.claim: Columnar whisker responses were weaker in enriched than normally housed mice in L4 (NH: 0.98 ± 0.09, EN: 0.81 ± 0.04, p=0.02).
claims.source: When receptive fields were examined in somatotopic space, CW responses were weaker in EN than NH (NH: 0.98 ± 0.09, EN: 0.81 ± 0.04, p=0.02), as were responses to the within-row, +one arc SW (NH: 0.54 ± 0.08, EN: 0.17 ± 0.02, p=0.0001), the within-row, −1 arc SW (NH: 0.67 ± 0.13, EN 0.33 ± 0.04, p=0.003), and the within-arc, +one row SW (NH: 0.23 ± 0.03, EN 0.11 ± 0.02, p=0.0007).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 receptive field analysis.

claims.claim: Enrichment sharpened L4 receptive fields by a global weakening of whisker responses, unlike in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, EN sharpened L4 receptive fields, but by a global weakening of whisker responses, unlike in L2/3.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion comparing enrichment effects in L4 versus L2/3.

claims.claim: The enrichment effect in L4 differs from adult enrichment in rats, which shrinks whisker receptive fields in L2/3 but not L4.
claims.source: This effect differs from adult enrichment in rats, which shrinks whisker receptive fields in L2/3 but not L4 (Polley et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to prior work cited from Polley et al., 2004.

claims.claim: Prior imaging studies detected a global tuning gradient in L2/3 of S1 but no functional boundaries at anatomical column edges.
claims.source: Prior imaging studies detected a global tuning gradient in L2/3 of S1 but no functional boundaries at anatomical column edges (Kerr et al., 2007; Sato et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior imaging studies.

claims.claim: In normally housed mice, mean signal correlation for L2/3 neuron pairs fell off modestly with intersoma distance.
claims.source: In NH mice, mean signal correlation for neuron pairs fell off modestly with intersoma distance, and was slightly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by signal correlation data in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: For closely spaced L2/3 pairs (<150 μm apart) in normally housed mice, signal correlation was only modestly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs (0.652 ± 0.005 vs. 0.611 ± 0.007, p<0.0001).
claims.source: For closely spaced pairs (<150 μm apart) signal correlation was only modestly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs (0.652 ± 0.005 vs. 0.611 ± 0.007, p<0.0001, permutation test of difference in means), reflecting the lack of functional column boundaries (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, mean signal correlation for within-column L2/3 pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
claims.source: In EN mice, mean signal correlation for within-column pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; includes pairs at all distances; p<0.0001, permutation test), while signal correlation for across-column pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001) (Figure 5A,C).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A,C.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, signal correlation for across-column L2/3 pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001).
claims.source: In EN mice, mean signal correlation for within-column pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; includes pairs at all distances; p<0.0001, permutation test), while signal correlation for across-column pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001) (Figure 5A,C).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A,C.

claims.claim: In enriched mice, signal correlation for closely spaced cross-column L2/3 pairs (<150 μm apart) was much lower than for similarly spaced within-column pairs (0.674 ± 0.003 vs. 0.529 ± 0.006, p<0.0001).
claims.source: Moreover, signal correlation for closely spaced cross-column pairs (<150 μm apart) was much lower than for similarly spaced within-column pairs (0.674 ± 0.003 vs. 0.529 ± 0.006, p<0.0001) (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Enrichment generated a tuning boundary at column edges in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, EN generated a tuning boundary at column edges.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the signal correlation data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Noise correlations measure shared, stimulus-independent trial-to-trial variability between neurons, likely reflecting shared functional input.
claims.source: EN also generated columnar structure in noise correlations, which measure shared, stimulus-independent trial-to-trial variability between neurons, likely reflecting shared functional input (Averbeck et al., 2006; Kohn et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on noise correlations.

claims.claim: In normally housed mice, noise correlations for L2/3 neuron pairs decreased with distance and were similar within columns (0.334 ± 0.002) and across columns (0.327 ± 0.002).
claims.source: In NH mice, noise correlations for L2/3 neuron pairs decreased with distance, and were similar within columns (0.334 ± 0.002) and across columns (0.327 ± 0.002).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis.

claims.claim: Enrichment modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column L2/3 pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001 vs. NH).
claims.source: EN modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH), but greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis shown in Figure 5B,D.

claims.claim: Enrichment greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column L2/3 pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001 vs. NH).
claims.source: EN modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH), but greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis shown in Figure 5B,D.

claims.claim: Enrichment substantially reduced signal and noise correlations for L2/3 neurons outside the reference column to neurons inside the column.
claims.source: In NH, neurons outside the reference column exhibited fairly high signal and noise correlations to the neurons inside the column. EN substantially reduced these signal and noise correlations for neurons outside the column, while preserving signal correlation and only modestly reducing noise correlation among neurons within the reference column (Figure 5E–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by spatial maps of correlations in Figure 5E-F.

claims.claim: Enrichment generated a stronger gradient of signal- and noise-correlation in L2/3 at the reference column edge.
claims.source: This generated a stronger gradient of signal- and noise-correlation in L2/3 at the reference column edge (Figure 5G–H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5G-H showing steeper correlation gradients.

claims.claim: In L4, enrichment generally increased correlations between co-columnar neurons.
claims.source: In L4 of Scnn1a-Cre mice, EN generally increased correlations between co-columnar neurons (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased signal correlations between co-columnar neurons in L4 (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001).
claims.source: This was true for both signal correlations (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001) and noise correlations (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 correlation analysis shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased noise correlations between co-columnar neurons in L4 (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
claims.source: This was true for both signal correlations (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001) and noise correlations (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 correlation analysis shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Enrichment drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, EN drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3, and increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation data in Figures 5 and 6.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
claims.source: Thus, EN drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3, and increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the L4 correlation data in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The major effects of enrichment were robust to different levels of neuropil correction in both L2/3 and L4.
claims.source: To confirm that the major effects of the study were robust to different levels of neuropil correction, we applied neuropil subtraction in both L2/3 and L4 at three weights (r = 0, r = 0.3, r = 0.7, see Materials and methods) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). Enrichment effects on tuning heterogeneity (Figure 3) and point representation (Figure 5) were qualitatively unchanged across these levels of neuropil subtraction in both L2/3 and L4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 testing robustness to methodological choices.

claims.claim: Enrichment improved detection of columnar whisker deflections by spatially clustered L2/3 pyramidal cell ensembles located in column centers.
claims.source: Enrichment improved detection of CW deflections by spatially clustered PYR ensembles located in column centers (Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This is supported by neural decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Enrichment increased both absolute detection accuracy and coding efficiency such that in enriched mice, smaller ensembles were needed for equivalent detection performance.
claims.source: Enrichment increased both absolute detection accuracy and coding efficiency such that in EN mice, smaller ensembles were needed for equivalent detection performance.
claims.evidence: This is supported by decoder performance data in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: The strengthening of columnar whisker-evoked responses, the reduction of spontaneous activity and noise correlations, and the higher proportion of columnar whisker-tuned neurons are sufficient to improve single-trial coding of whisker deflections in enriched mice.
claims.source: Thus, the strengthening of CW-evoked responses, the reduction of spontaneous activity and noise correlations, and the higher proportion of CW-tuned neurons are sufficient to improve single-trial coding of whisker deflections in EN mice.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Enrichment improved detection by ensembles in the home whisker column, but worsened detection by ensembles in neighboring columns.
claims.source: Topographically, enrichment improved detection by ensembles in the home whisker column, but worsened detection by ensembles in neighboring columns (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by decoder performance as a function of distance in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: The columnar organization of effective decoding was sharpened by enrichment, matching the sharper point representations in L2/3 of enriched S1.
claims.source: Thus, the columnar organization of effective decoding was sharpened, matching the sharper point representations in L2/3 of enriched S1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: The dispersed, salt-and-pepper, weakly columnar somatotopy in L2/3 of S1 is partially a product of impoverished experience in standard laboratory housing.
claims.source: These results indicate that the dispersed, salt-and-pepper, weakly columnar somatotopy in L2/3 of S1 is partially a product of impoverished experience in standard laboratory housing.
claims.evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the enrichment effects observed.

claims.claim: Salt-and-pepper organization is a robust feature of rodent L2/3 sensory maps, but its degree is flexible based on experience.
claims.source: Enrichment reduced, but did not eliminate, salt-and-pepper tuning heterogeneity in L2/3. Thus, salt-and-pepper organization is a robust feature of rodent L2/3 sensory maps, but its degree is flexible based on experience.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding that enrichment reduced but did not abolish salt-and-pepper organization.

claims.claim: Columns became more functionally independent after enrichment, which predicts more accurate column-based encoding of whisker input.
claims.source: Enrichment reduced both mean tuning similarity and stimulus-independent (spontaneous) firing correlations across columns. Thus, columns became more functionally independent, which predicts more accurate column-based encoding of whisker input.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation data and decoder analysis.

claims.claim: GCaMP6s was expressed conditionally in layer-specific neurons using Cre lines.
claims.source: We then characterized whisker tuning and somatotopic map organization in L2/3 or L4 excitatory cells using 2-photon imaging of GCaMP6s expressed conditionally using layer-specific Cre lines.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claims.claim: Enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1.
claims.source: Thus, enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1, so that cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map.
claims.evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the enrichment effects observed.

claims.claim: After enrichment, cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map in L2/3.
claims.source: Thus, enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1, so that cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map.
claims.evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study.

claims.claim: Whisker-evoked ΔF/F responses were measured from regions of interest corresponding to GCaMP6-expressing somata.
claims.source: Whisker-evoked ΔF/F responses were measured from regions of interest (ROI) corresponding to GCaMP6-expressing somata.
claims.evidence: This describes the measurement method used in the study.

claims.claim: ROIs were considered significantly whisker-responsive if the distribution of whisker-evoked ΔF/F was greater than blank trials (permutation test, α = 0.05 corrected for nine whiskers).
claims.source: ROIs were considered significantly whisker-responsive if the distribution of whisker-evoked ΔF/F (quantified in a 1 s period after whisker deflection) was greater than blank trials (permutation test, α = 0.05 corrected for nine whiskers, see Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: This describes the statistical criterion for identifying responsive neurons.

claims.claim: Imaged neurons were localized post-hoc relative to column boundaries by histological staining and alignment by surface blood vessels.
claims.source: Imaged neurons were localized post-hoc relative to column boundaries by histological staining and alignment by surface blood vessels (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This describes the method for localizing neurons to anatomical columns.

claims.claim: Enriched mice were housed with 2–3 littermates in standard mouse cages with nesting enclosure and several toys that were exchanged every 2–4 days.
claims.source: EN animals were housed with 2–3 littermates in standard mouse cages (30 × 14 × 18 cm) into which a nesting enclosure and several toys were added and exchanged every 2–4 days.
claims.evidence: This describes the enrichment housing protocol.

claims.claim: Toys included sticks and blocks made from wood, ridged plastic, PVC, rubber, or cement, chosen for diversity of shape and texture.
claims.source: Toys included sticks and blocks made from wood, ridged plastic, PVC, rubber, or cement, chosen for diversity of shape and texture (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1–).
claims.evidence: This describes the types of enrichment toys used.

claims.claim: Normally housed mice were housed with one littermate and no toys.
claims.source: NH mice were housed in the same cage, with one littermate and no toys.
claims.evidence: This describes the normal housing protocol.

claims.claim: A single surgery for headgear implant and viral injection was performed at approximately P41 for Drd3-Cre mice or approximately P30 for Scnn1a-Cre mice.
claims.source: A single surgery for headgear implant and viral injection was performed at ~P41 (Drd3-Cre mice) or ~P30 (Scnn1a-Cre mice).
claims.evidence: This describes the surgical timeline.

claims.claim: Intrinsic signal imaging was performed through the intact skull to localize D1, D2 and D3 columns in S1.
claims.source: Intrinsic signal imaging (ISOI) was performed through the intact skull to localize D1, D2 and D3 columns in S1 (Drew and Feldman, 2009), and a 3 mm craniotomy was made over the D2 column.
claims.evidence: This describes the method for localizing barrel columns before surgery.

claims.claim: For L2/3 imaging in Drd3-Cre mice, AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE was injected at approximately 200 and 300 µm below the dura.
claims.source: For L2/3 (Drd3-Cre mice), we used AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE, injected at ~200 and ~300 µm below the dura.
claims.evidence: This describes the viral injection protocol for L2/3 labeling.

claims.claim: For L4 imaging in Scnn1a-Cre mice, AAV9-CAG-Flex-GCaMP6s-WPRE was injected at approximately 350 and 450 µm below the dura.
claims.source: For L4 (Scnn1a-Cre mice), we used AAV9-CAG-Flex-GCaMP6s-WPRE, injected ~350 and ~450 µm below the dura.
claims.evidence: This describes the viral injection protocol for L4 labeling.

claims.claim: Mice recovered to pre-surgical weight within 4 days (normally housed) or 5.5 days (enriched), on average.
claims.source: Mice recovered to pre-surgical weight within 4 days (NH) or 5.5 days (EN), on average.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from surgical recovery monitoring.

claims.claim: The prevalence of exploratory behaviors did not differ between enriched and normally housed mice during surgical recovery.
claims.source: The prevalence of these behaviors did not differ between EN and NH mice, although EN mice showed a non-significant trend for more locomotor behavior (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is a result from behavioral monitoring during recovery.

claims.claim: Imaging was performed under low-dose isoflurane (<1% in oxygen) combined with the sedative chlorprothixene (0.08 mg, i.p.).
claims.source: Imaging was performed under low-dose isoflurane (<1% in oxygen) combined with the sedative chlorprothixene (0.08 mg, i.p.), with body temperature stabilized at 37°C.
claims.evidence: This describes the anesthesia protocol for imaging.

claims.claim: L2/3 imaging fields were approximately 400 × 400 μm, located approximately 100–250 µm below the dura, and contained approximately 50–100 expressing neurons.

results.result: In normally housed mice, L2/3 exhibits dispersed salt-and-pepper whisker tuning with only 67% of neurons tuned to their columnar whisker, while L4 shows sharper topography with 73% columnar tuning and ~30% steeper spatial falloff of tuning with distance.
results.evaluation: Multiple converging lines of evidence support this result: quantitative tuning analysis (C49-C51), spatial distribution analysis (C52), and imaging data from both layers (C3-C4, C38, C43). Statistical tests (Fisher's Exact Test, permutation tests) with appropriate corrections are applied. The comparison between L2/3 and L4 is internally consistent and aligns with prior literature (C140-C141).

results.result: Enrichment sharpened whisker point representations in L2/3 by increasing responses in the home column (0-300 μm: p<0.01) and suppressing responses at flanks (375-750 μm: p<0.05), while increasing the fraction of columnar-whisker-tuned neurons from 65.1% to 77.1% (p=0.00008), though salt-and-pepper organization persisted.
results.evaluation: The result is well-supported by quantitative spatial analysis with appropriate statistical tests (C40-C41, C54-C55), imaging data from multiple fields (C39, C42), and consistent conclusions across multiple claims (C5-C7, C56, C101-C102). The persistence of salt-and-pepper organization (C6, C56) appropriately qualifies the main finding. Sample sizes are adequate (11 fields per condition, 7 mice per group).

results.result: Enrichment increased tuning precision in L4 by globally weakening whisker responses rather than selectively enhancing columnar responses, increasing columnar tuning from 75.6% to 89.3% (p=0.0086), which differs from prior adult enrichment studies in rats.
results.evaluation: The L4 effects are well-documented with quantitative measurements (C44, C57-C58, C70) and appropriate statistical tests. The mechanistic interpretation (global weakening vs. selective enhancement, C45, C71) is supported by rank-ordered receptive field analysis (C68-C69). The comparison to prior work (C72, C157) appropriately contextualizes the findings, though species/age differences limit direct comparison.

results.result: Enrichment sharpened L2/3 receptive fields by increasing signal-to-noise for the strongest whiskers, decreasing spontaneous activity, strengthening columnar whisker responses (NH: 0.64±0.03, EN: 0.71±0.02; p=0.01), and creating anisotropic sharpening (reduced across-row responses but increased rostral within-row responses).
results.evaluation: The receptive field analysis is comprehensive with rank-ordered analysis (C60-C61), signal-to-noise quantification (C62), spontaneous activity measurement (C63), and somatotopic decomposition (C64-C67). Statistical tests are appropriate (permutation tests) with clear p-values. The anisotropic sharpening (C67) is an important nuance supported by directional analysis (C65-C66).

results.result: Enrichment created functional column boundaries in L2/3 by modestly increasing within-column signal correlation (NH: 0.637±0.004, EN: 0.659±0.002; p<0.0001) while greatly reducing across-column signal correlation (NH: 0.541±0.004, EN: 0.425±0.004; p<0.0001), generating sharp tuning boundaries at column edges that were absent in normally housed mice.
results.evaluation: The signal correlation analysis is rigorous with large sample sizes (thousands of cell pairs), appropriate statistical tests (permutation tests), and spatial analysis showing correlation gradients (C84-C85). The comparison to prior work (C73) establishes novelty. The distinction between within- and across-column effects (C76-C78) is critical and well-supported. The conclusion about functional boundaries (C79, C89) follows logically from the data.

results.result: Enrichment reduced noise correlations in L2/3, with modest reduction within columns (NH: 0.334±0.002, EN: 0.307±0.001; p<0.0001) but large reduction across columns (NH: 0.327±0.002, EN: 0.255±0.001; p<0.0001), indicating reduced shared trial-to-trial variability between columns.
results.evaluation: The noise correlation analysis parallels the signal correlation analysis with appropriate methodology (C80, C130) and statistical rigor (C82-C83). The interpretation regarding shared functional input (C80) is supported by citations. The differential effects within vs. across columns are consistent with the signal correlation findings, strengthening the overall conclusion about functional column emergence.

results.result: In L4, enrichment increased both signal correlations (NH: 0.681±0.011, EN: 0.774±0.005; p<0.0001) and noise correlations (NH: 0.241±0.006, EN: 0.356±0.002; p<0.0001) within columns, indicating increased coordinated activity within each barrel.
results.evaluation: The L4 correlation analysis shows opposite effects from L2/3, which is biologically interesting and well-supported by quantitative data (C87-C88). Statistical tests are appropriate. However, the interpretation regarding mechanisms (C90, C167) is somewhat speculative. The lack of cross-column analysis in L4 (noted in text) is a limitation but doesn't undermine the within-column findings.

results.result: Enrichment improved neural population coding of whisker deflections, with better detection performance for ensembles ≥3 neurons (p<0.001) and spatially sharpened decoding such that ensembles in the home column (0-154 μm) showed improved detection while neighboring column ensembles showed reduced detection.
results.evaluation: The decoder analysis provides functional validation of the map changes using appropriate machine learning methods (logistic regression, cross-validation, C131-C132). Performance improvements are statistically significant (C133-C134) and spatially specific (C95, C135). The conclusion that map changes improve coding (C94, C138, C172) is supported, though the caveat about behavioral relevance (C171) is appropriately noted.

results.result: GCaMP6s-based receptive fields were validated against spike recordings in 9/10 L2/3 neurons, though GCaMP measurements differ from spike-based measurements due to lower single-spike sensitivity, train stimuli, and potential tangential activity propagation within the 1s response window.
results.evaluation: The validation experiment (C34) provides critical methodological support, though the 9/10 success rate indicates some limitations. The discussion of methodological differences (C142-C143) is appropriately cautious. The justification for using imaging (C144) is sound. However, the potential confounds (tangential propagation, C143) could affect interpretation of salt-and-pepper organization, which is acknowledged but not fully resolved.

results.result: Enrichment did not alter anatomical barrel radius in either Drd3-Cre mice (NH: 151±7.2 μm, EN: 145±4.6 μm, p=0.7) or Scnn1a-Cre mice (NH: 118±6.6 μm, EN: 124±6.9 μm, p=0.01), indicating functional changes occurred without gross anatomical reorganization.
results.evaluation: The anatomical measurements (C46-C47) use appropriate statistics (2-way ANOVA) and adequate sample sizes (5-7 mice per group). The conclusion (C48) appropriately distinguishes functional from anatomical changes. However, the p=0.01 for Scnn1a-Cre mice (C47) is stated as showing "no change," which is inconsistent with the p-value, though the effect size appears small.

results.result: The major enrichment effects on tuning heterogeneity and point representation were robust to different levels of neuropil correction (r=0, 0.3, 0.7) in both L2/3 and L4, though signal correlation effects were lost at highest correction level (r=0.7) due to reduced cell numbers.
results.evaluation: The robustness analysis (C91) is important for validating methodological choices. Testing three correction levels is thorough. The loss of signal correlation effects at r=0.7 is appropriately attributed to reduced statistical power rather than a true effect, which is a reasonable interpretation. This strengthens confidence in the main findings.

results.result: The experimental design used layer-specific Cre lines (Drd3-Cre for L2/3, Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre for L4) to express GCaMP6s, enrichment from P21 for 25-50 days with tactile toys exchanged every 2-4 days, and 2-photon imaging under anesthesia with 9-whisker stimulation (5-pulse trains, 60±10 repetitions per whisker).
results.evaluation: The methods are clearly described with appropriate detail (C30-C33, C106-C120). The enrichment protocol (C35-C37, C106-C108) is well-defined. Surgical recovery was monitored and similar between groups (C113-C114). The use of train stimuli (C117-C118) is justified by L2/3 physiology. However, the enrichment includes multiple factors (tactile, social, activity) that cannot be disentangled (C173-C174), which is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

results.result: The dispersed salt-and-pepper organization in L2/3 is partially a product of impoverished laboratory housing experience, as enrichment reduced but did not eliminate it, suggesting salt-and-pepper organization is a robust but experience-modulated feature of rodent sensory maps.
results.evaluation: This is the central conceptual conclusion of the paper (C97-C98), well-supported by the experimental findings. The interpretation is appropriately nuanced ("partially," "reduced but not eliminated"). The predictions about coding efficiency (C99, C163-C165) are supported by the decoder analysis.
